parameters.content:
## 0) Check the ticket is not already solved or closed

Runs first, and on purpose does NOT post an internal note or reopen the ticket.

Why the guard: on 2026-07-23 Zendesk redelivered a `ticket created` webhook 8h37m late. The automation re-ran on the original first email, found the refundable charges already consumed, and emailed the customer a refund rejection after having already granted the refund.

Why no internal note here: the shared `Do not proceed` path sets the ticket back to `open`. On a solved ticket that would re-queue it for agents and could re-fire the 2nd-message trigger.

Why base `status` and not a `cs_project_config` id: the ticket API always returns `status` as a plain string, so no new column is needed and `closed` is covered for free.

parameters.content:
# Second message / follow-up path

This check runs on customer REPLIES inside an existing ticket, not on first contact.

**Deliberately NOT here** (all of them belong to first contact only, and are handled by `Request eligibility check with merging (first message)`):
- requester lookup + requested-tickets fetch
- the active-ticket guard and duplicate merge - by definition the customer is replying inside an active ticket, so merging could close the very ticket they are conversing in
- the AI spam check - already cleared on message one, and a terse follow-up ("ANY UPDATE???") is its worst false-positive shape

**Bug removed 2026-08-27:** the old `Evaluate Open Ticket Guard` counted ANY other requester ticket regardless of status, including solved and closed ones for 120 days. It suppressed automation for essentially every repeat customer, wrote an internal note calling closed tickets "unhandled (new)", and flipped pending tickets back to open. Every label on it said "new tickets" - only the code disagreed.

**What remains:** status guard, blocklist, auto-solve list, contact-form cancellation. Four cheap checks, no AI, no user lookup.

nodes.name: High risk check enabled?
nodes.notes: cs_project_config.high_risk_check_enabled. Empty or false = OFF (opt-in).

nodes.name: Get last customer comment
nodes.notes: On the follow-up path the ticket's description is still the ORIGINAL message, so it cannot be used for matching. The new text lives in the latest customer comment and has to be fetched. This runs here rather than later in the 2nd message flow so that tickets dropped by the message-limit and classification gates are still covered.

nodes.name: Extract last customer comment
nodes.notes: Newest comment authored by the requester. Matching only the NEW text is deliberate: matching the whole thread would re-flag the same ticket on every follow-up, and the original message was already checked by the first-message eligibility check.

nodes.name: Get High Risk Keywords
nodes.notes: cs_high_risk_keywords. GLOBAL - no project_key column. One phrase list for every brand; only the check itself is per-project.

nodes.name: Build high risk payload
nodes.notes: In monitoring mode only the tag and note are sent - no status change, no allow_automation change, and the ticket continues into automation.

nodes.name: High risk enforce?
nodes.notes: True = stop automation. False = monitoring mode, fall through to the contact-form check and carry on as normal.

nodes.name: Do not proceed (high risk)
nodes.notes: Same return shape as every other terminal. The note, tag and status were already written by Zendesk: Flag high risk, so this does NOT route through the shared loud-fail path.

parameters.content:
## High-risk keyword check (follow-up path)

Runs after the blocklist and auto-solve tables, before the contact-form check.

**Why here and not later in the 2nd message flow,** where `Return last comment` already has the text: the message-limit threshold, the allow_automation filter and the classification gate all drop tickets SILENTLY further downstream. A safety phrase in message 8 of a long thread would never be seen. Those excluded tickets are disproportionately the long, escalating, repeat-contact threads this check exists for. The price is one extra Zendesk call per follow-up.

**Matches the LATEST CUSTOMER COMMENT, not the ticket description.** On this path the description is still the original first message, which the first-message check already evaluated. Matching the whole thread would also re-flag the same ticket on every reply.

`Extract last customer comment` walks backwards to the newest comment whose `author_id` is the requester, so agent replies and the automation's own internal notes are skipped - otherwise we would match the keyword quoted inside our own note.

**Table:** `cs_high_risk_keywords`. Global, no `project_key`. Rows switched on and off with `active`.

**Matching:** normalise both sides, then token-sequence match anchored with `(^| )needle( |$)`. Tier precedence **C > A > B**. Every match is listed in the note, not just the winner.

**Two switches in cs_project_config:**
- `high_risk_check_enabled` - master on/off, per project, opt-in
- `high_risk_enforce` - OFF = monitoring (tag + note only, bot still replies), ON = tag + note + status open + `allow_automation _no_` + automation stops

nodes.name: RR: Repeat refusal enabled?
nodes.notes: cs_project_config.record_checks_enabled. Empty or false = OFF (opt-in), same convention as the high-risk check.

nodes.name: RR: Evaluate reopens
nodes.notes: No extra API call - the metric set is sideloaded onto the existing Get ticket status read.

nodes.name: RR: Build payload
nodes.notes: In tag-only mode only the tag and note are sent - no status change, no allow_automation change, and the ticket continues into automation.

nodes.name: RR: Enforce?
nodes.notes: True = stop automation. False = monitoring mode, fall through to the contact-form check and carry on as normal.

nodes.name: Do not proceed (repeat refusal)
nodes.notes: Same return shape as every other terminal. The note, tag and status were already written by RR: Zendesk flag repeat refusal, so this does NOT route through the shared loud-fail path.

parameters.content:
## Record-based case 7b - repeated refusal of the automated resolution

Runs after the high-risk keyword check, before the contact-form check. All three
high-risk exits funnel in here, so the check is reached whether or not the
high-risk block ran.

**Signal:** Zendesk's `reopens` counter - solved -> open transitions on this
ticket. Verified on Personality 2026-09: every reopen examined was caused by the
requester replying; the automation never reopens a ticket it solved.

**Why not "count the customer's replies":** the automation also sends
NON-resolution public replies. The password_account_info macros ask the customer
for their account email and leave the ticket PENDING. A customer answering that
is cooperating, not refusing. Pending is not a solve, so it produces no reopen
and those customers are excluded for free.

**Cost:** no extra API call. `?include=metric_sets` was added to the existing
Get ticket status read.

**Known limitation:** a thank-you also reopens a solved ticket. At a threshold of
2 this mostly washes out, because gratitude is terminal and refusal repeats.
A customer who pushes back once and gives up will NOT flag - under-flagging is
the intended direction.

**Two switches in cs_project_config:**
- `record_checks_enabled` - master on/off, per project, opt-in
- `record_checks_enforce` - OFF = monitoring (tag + note only), ON = tag + note +
  status open + `allow_automation _no_` + automation stops
- `record_repeat_refusal_threshold` - reopens needed to fire. Defaults to 2.
